After working through the Hugging Face course, I fine-tuned a **DistilBERT encoder** for binary text classification and published it as [polkas/educational-story-outcome-predictor](https://huggingface.co/polkas/educational-story-outcome-predictor).

The model takes two text inputs: an educational situation and the proposed solution. It predicts a **Success** or **Failure** label derived from the story's outcome annotations. This is supervised classification, not a demonstration that the model can establish an intervention's effectiveness.

## Model and data

- **Architecture:** pretrained `distilbert-base-uncased`, fine-tuned with a classification head; approximately 67 million parameters.
- **Inputs:** situation text, combining the description and background, paired with the solution text.
- **Dataset:** [Edustories-en](https://huggingface.co/datasets/MU-NLPC/Edustories-en), containing 1,492 annotated entries. The reported run retained 1,471 after filtering.
- **Training:** the model card reports approximately five minutes on Apple Silicon.

The binary label mapping groups partial, short-term and long-term success annotations into **Success** and maps the remaining categories to **Failure**. It simplifies the original annotations rather than measuring an outcome directly.

## Reported evaluation

The [model card](https://huggingface.co/polkas/educational-story-outcome-predictor) reports a stratified split with 882 training, 221 validation and 368 test entries.

| Metric | Reported result |
|---|---:|
| Model accuracy | 74.18% |
| F1 for the Success class | 82.18% |
| Precision for the Success class | 71.80% |
| Recall for the Success class | 96.05% |
| Majority-class baseline accuracy | 61.96% |

These are results from one split, not evidence of general educational decision-making performance. The dataset can contain multiple annotations of the same story, while the training script splits rows rather than grouping by story identifier. A story-grouped evaluation would be needed to assess generalisation to independent stories.

## Community recognition

[Jan Nehyba](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jan-nehyba-55a38341/), one of the dataset's curators at Masaryk University, highlighted the project on LinkedIn as an example of open educational data being used to build an NLP application.
